subject: Re: Escalation playbook refresh — Platform ownership boundaries + escalation contacts
body:
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 9, 2026 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Escalation playbook refresh — Platform ownership boundaries + escalation contacts

Hi Priya,

We’re finalizing the Confluence page for escalation paths/contacts (targeting publish EOD Tue). Can you confirm Platform ownership boundaries + who Support should page for the following buckets?

Buckets we want to be explicit about (so Support doesn’t shotgun-page the wrong team):
- SSO/SAML/SCIM issues (Console login loops, SAML config changes, SCIM sync)
- Quota / rate-limit enforcement and headers (429 confusion, account limits vs header reporting)
- Audit logs (delivery latency, missing events, export pipeline)
- Routing / fallback behavior (model pinning + fallback policy confusion, tier-aware routing)

Also: preferred escalation contact(s) + backup, and any “always include” info (org id, request ids, region, etc.) so on-call can triage quickly.

Thanks — this will go verbatim into the escalation matrix.

— Dev Patel
Support Ops | Redwood Inference



From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 9, 2026 at 10:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: Escalation playbook refresh — Platform ownership boundaries + escalation contacts

Dev — yes, thank you for making this explicit.

High-level ownership boundaries (Platform):

1) SSO / SAML / SCIM / Console auth flows
- Owner: Platform Control Plane (Auth/Identity)
- When to page: customer cannot log into Console; SAML/SCIM changes are blocked; widespread login loop; admin lockout; “all users” impact at a customer.
- Not Platform: client-side SDK auth errors (401/403 on API calls) where the customer is using an invalid key — those stay in Support triage unless you see a systemic auth outage.

2) Quota + rate limits (limits enforcement, account entitlements, rate-limit headers)
- Owner: Platform Control Plane (Usage/Entitlements)
- When to page: unexpected 429 spike not explained by limits; inconsistent headers across endpoints; suspected misclassification of 429 vs quota exhaustion; contract entitlement mismatch.
- Not Platform: customer-side retry storms or concurrency spikes (still Support-led, page SRE if broad impact / service health issue).

3) Audit logs (delivery pipeline + export)
- Owner: Platform Control Plane (Audit/Compliance pipeline)
- When to page: audit logs delayed beyond enterprise expectation, missing events for a time window, export job failures.
- Not Platform: customer’s downstream SIEM ingestion failures (Support can advise, page Platform only if our export delivery is failing).

4) Routing / fallback behavior
- “Routing decisions / fallback activation / tier-aware routing” is owned by the Routing subteam (within Platform org, but separate on-call).
- “Serving/runtime” issues (model-specific 5xx, perf regressions due to runtime changes) go to SRE + Runtime on-call per standard incident process.
- When to page Routing: customer reporting pinned version confusion, unexpected model variant, cross-region routing questions, fallback policy interpretation.

Escalation contacts (what Support should use in the playbook):
- Primary entry point (Platform): PagerDuty schedule “Platform - Control Plane Oncall” (use paging group; do not DM individuals)
- Routing: PagerDuty schedule “Platform - Routing Oncall”
- Slack: #help-platform for async, #platform-oncall for active escalation coordination once paged

Always include in the page / escalation summary:
- Customer org ID + tier (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
- Region(s)
- Time window (with timezone)
- Request IDs (2–5 examples)
- API key prefix (first 6 chars) OR Console workspace URL (no full secrets)
- Impact statement: number of users / endpoints / severity + whether customer blocked

I’ll send a tighter snippet you can paste into Confluence once I sanity-check the PD schedule names.

— Priya
VP Engineering, Platform | Redwood Inference



From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Escalation playbook refresh — Platform ownership boundaries + escalation contacts

+1 to the above.

Two SRE notes for the playbook wording:

- For anything that looks like “multi-customer” or “regional” impact (elevated 5xx, auth outage, widespread latency), Support should move to the incident pathway (#incidents + SRE on-call) rather than staying solely in #support/#help-platform. Platform can be pulled in from there.

- Please avoid language that implies Support should bypass PD and ping people directly. We’ve had a few cases where a DM didn’t wake the right on-call.

If you want, I can provide a single sentence for the escalation matrix like: “If suspected platform-wide impact: page SRE first; SRE will pull Platform/Routing.”

— Sean
SRE | Redwood Inference

This is great.

Quick follow-up on quota/rate-limit: for the current “header mismatch” theme (429s + inconsistent X-RateLimit-*), should Support treat that as Platform Control Plane on-call first, or go straight to the existing Eng ticket (ENG-4825) / file a SUP escalation and let Control Plane triage?

Trying to avoid confusion where Support thinks it’s a generic “service degradation” and pages SRE, when it’s actually an entitlement/header edge case.

Also confirming: for audit log lag, are we OK stating an expected delivery window in the playbook (e.g., “normally <5 min; page Platform if >30 min for enterprise”) or do you want that to live only in the SLA mapping doc?

— Dev

Subject: Re: Escalation playbook refresh — Platform ownership boundaries + escalation contacts

Dev — guidance below (paste-ready for Confluence).

---
PLATFORM OWNERSHIP (Support Escalation Matrix)

SSO / SAML / SCIM (Console login + identity)
- Owning team: Platform Control Plane (Identity)
- Page: PD “Platform - Control Plane Oncall”
- Slack: #help-platform (async), #platform-oncall (once paged)
- Escalate when: customer admin(s) blocked, login loop, SAML/SCIM changes blocked, suspected Redwood-side auth regression
- Include: IdP type (Okta/AAD/etc.), SAML metadata timestamp (if changed), Console workspace URL, error screenshots OK (no secrets)

Quota / Rate limits / Entitlements (429s, header consistency)
- Owning team: Platform Control Plane (Usage/Entitlements)
- Page: PD “Platform - Control Plane Oncall”
- Escalate when: unexpected 429 spike not explained by usage, inconsistent headers, suspected misclassification (quota vs rate-limit)
- Note: If symptoms coincide with elevated 5xx/latency across customers/regions, treat as incident and page SRE first.
- Workflow: file/attach a SUP ticket + link ENG-4825 if it matches the known edge case; Control Plane on-call triages/assigns.

Audit logs (delivery latency, missing events, export failures)
- Owning team: Platform Control Plane (Audit/Compliance)
- Page: PD “Platform - Control Plane Oncall”
- Escalate when: enterprise customer reports sustained lag or missing events; export job failures on our side
- Avoid hard numbers in the escalation playbook. Point to the SLA/SLO mapping page for thresholds.

Routing / Fallback / Model pinning behavior
- Owning team: Platform Routing
- Page: PD “Platform - Routing Oncall”
- Escalate when: customer believes pinned model/version not respected, unexpected fallback, cross-region routing questions
- Note: runtime/model quality/perf regressions → incident path (SRE + runtime) unless Routing confirms it’s policy/config only.

REQUIRED CONTEXT FOR ANY PLATFORM PAGE
- Org ID + tier (Hosted/Dedicated/Private/Enterprise)
- Region(s)
- Time window (include timezone)
- 2–5 request IDs + endpoint(s)
- Impact statement (blocked vs degraded; single customer vs suspected broad)
- Any recent change noted by customer (SDK upgrade, SAML config change, rollout window)

---

Re: audit log expected window: agree with keeping numeric thresholds out of the escalation directory so we don’t accidentally contradict contracts. We can say “unexpected delay” + “enterprise sensitivity” and link to the SLA/SLO mapping doc for the concrete paging trigger.

Re: header mismatch theme: have Support open/attach a SUP escalation and link ENG-4825. Platform Control Plane on-call should be first-page unless there’s evidence of broader service health (then SRE first as Sean noted).

Thanks — this should make triage/paging cleaner.

— Priya
VP Engineering, Platform | Redwood Inference
